keyVerseText: And from thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the LORD spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew root בְּאֵר (bᵉʼêr, H875) fundamentally signifies a pit or well, emphasizing a source of water drawn from beneath the earth. This root meaning highlights not just any water source, but one that is dug or naturally occurring as a spring or pit, distinguishing it from surface water. The noun בְּאֵר (Bᵉʼêr, H876) carries this foundational idea forward, referring specifically to a well or oasis, a vital place of refreshment and sustenance in arid regions.
usageInScripture: The word בְּאֵר appears twice in Scripture, consistently translated as 'Beer' in reference to a specific location. Both uses identify it as a geographical site, notably an oasis or well in the desert encountered during the Exodus and a city west of Hebron. This consistency in translation underscores its identity as a known place where water—a symbol of life and provision—is present, reinforcing the literal meaning of a well or spring as a crucial refuge for the people of Israel.
theologicalSignificance: The concept of בְּאֵר as a well or oasis carries deep theological weight, symbolizing God's provision and faithfulness to His people in times of need. In the wilderness context, a well represents sustenance and divine care amid scarcity, echoing the spiritual nourishment God offers to His followers. Recognizing בְּאֵר as both a physical and symbolic source of life invites believers to trust in God's ongoing provision through Christ, the living water who satisfies the deepest thirsts of the soul. This word reminds us that just as God provided water in the desert, He also provides salvation and sustenance for eternal life.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 21:16 states, 'And from thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the LORD spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water.' Here, בְּאֵר is not merely a place name but the very well promised by God, signifying His direct intervention to meet the Israelites' physical needs. The word 'Beer' enriches the verse by emphasizing God's faithful provision of water, a tangible blessing that sustains life and demonstrates His covenantal care. This well becomes a powerful reminder of God's promise to provide and sustain His people in their journey.
